purpose: Precision-only replication of the frozen v4 calendar-time self-normalized calibration. v4 returned INCONCLUSIVE (22 PASS, 2 INCONCLUSIVE, 0 FAIL): two H21 / 78-week cells were too close to the 0.95 coverage floor for 2,000 replicates to certify under the predeclared exact Clopper-Pearson rule. v5 changes ONLY the protocol identity, the seed and the replicate count; the method, DGPs, statistics, thresholds and decision rule are v4's, byte for byte. This is a calibration replication, not Alpha model v5, and not a historical experiment.

precisionCriterion.statement: The 95% Monte Carlo half-width of a probability estimate at p = 0.95 must be at most 0.5 percentage points, by BOTH the normal approximation and the exact two-sided Clopper-Pearson interval; the budget is the smallest multiple of 500 satisfying both.
precisionCriterion.normalApproximationFormula: z_0.975 * sqrt(p (1 - p) / R) <= targetHalfWidth, with z_0.975 = 1.959963984... (the exact 97.5th normal percentile, scipy norm.ppf(0.975), not the rounded 1.96)
precisionCriterion.exactRule: k = round(0.95 R) successes; half-width of the exact two-sided 95% interval; criterion holds for every larger R checked
precisionCriterion.derivedBy: pipeline.alpha_inference_calibration_v5.chosen_replicates (recomputed and asserted by the formal validator)
precisionCriterion.notDerivedFrom: any v4 cell, coverage value, exact Gaussian coverage or the number of cells that would classify

simulationReplicatesRationale: R = 8,000 follows from a general precision rule stated about a probability estimate at the coverage floor, not about any registered cell: the 95% Monte Carlo half-width at p = 0.95 must be at most 0.5pp. The normal approximation needs R >= 7,299; the exact Clopper-Pearson half-width at 7,500 is 0.0050001 (over target by 1.3e-7) and first meets the target at 7,501, so the smallest multiple of 500 satisfying both is 8,000. At 8,000 replicates PASS needs at least 7,639 covered (0.9549) and FAIL at most 7,526 (0.9408); the generic threshold-neighbourhood operating characteristic is in the precision diagnostics. A true coverage inside the remaining inconclusive band (about 0.941-0.955) is still expected to classify INCONCLUSIVE, and that is an honest statement of what 8,000 replicates can resolve; R is not raised further.

replicationOf.relationship: same method, same DGPs, same statistics, same thresholds, same decision rule; independent seed; larger budget; v4 draws are not reused

engineIdentity.rule: v5 CALLS the v4 engine; it does not copy it. The runner verifies the sha256 of every file the engine executes against these pins before any simulation.

confidence.multiplicity: Bonferroni over the two KR horizon primary expected-return claims, unchanged from v1-v3. Every confirmatory statistic in every cell is evaluated at the claim-level 97.5% interval; the calibration verdict is a conjunction over all of them, so no statistic or cell is an independent opportunity to pass.

minimumConfirmatoryDepth.rule: Confirmatory inference at a horizon is licensed only at evaluation calendars at least as deep as the shallowest depth this frozen calibration evaluated for that horizon. Shallower calendars were never calibrated and are DATA_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_CONFIRMATORY_H{horizon}_INFERENCE; they are never unlocked by a different interval.

dgpRationale.inherited: The four v1-v3 DGPs are kept byte-for-byte in their outcome parameters; none is removed.
dgpRationale.persistentPredictors: Under the v1-v3 null every predictor and selection score was redrawn independently each week, which makes rankIC, pairedMseImprovement and selectedMinusUniverse exact martingale-difference sequences whatever the overlap: they could not fail for the reason dateMean did. Real v5 scores persist week to week. phiPredictor 0.95 is a weekly AR(1) on each synthetic name's scores (a half-life of about 13.5 weeks), fixed a priori as a slow-moving-score stress, never estimated from data. Predictors remain independent of every return innovation, so the null is still exact.
dgpRationale.heavyTails: Student-t innovations with 4 degrees of freedom, rescaled to unit variance, applied to shared and idiosyncratic daily innovations: the heaviest integer tail with a finite variance and finite 2+delta moments, which the functional central limit theorem behind the self-normalized pivot requires.

nullConstruction.outcome: Forward sums of synthetic daily shared plus idiosyncratic shocks over exactly H sessions, sampled every five sessions.
nullConstruction.predictors: Generated from a separately spawned RNG stream and independent of every return innovation; weekly AR(1) with coefficient phiPredictor and unit stationary variance.
nullConstruction.pairedForecastContrast: Two exchangeable independent synthetic forecast streams with the same scale; expected paired MSE difference is exactly zero by symmetry.
nullConstruction.selection: Top 20 percent of names by an independent synthetic selection score, frozen at the signal date for the whole holding window.
nullConstruction.rankStatistic: Within-date Spearman correlation between an independent synthetic score and the forward target; population value is zero.
nullConstruction.rankWeightedSpread: Within-date return of a dollar-neutral portfolio weighted by centred ranks of the same independent score (long leg sums to one); population value is zero.

statistics.rationale: A statistic is confirmatory only if it is LINEAR in forward returns with weights fixed at the signal date (plus, for the MSE contrast, a forecast-only term known at the signal date), because only then can each realized return be attributed to the one calendar week in which it occurs. Spearman rankIC ranks the forward target, is not decomposable, and under persistent predictors inherits the full overlap dependence that v3's failure diagnosis identifies; it is reported with the v3 interval as a descriptive diagnostic and can neither pass nor fail the protocol. rankWeightedSpread is the decomposable, return-unit counterpart of a within-date ordering claim; whether v5 adopts it in place of Spearman rankIC is a v5 design decision this protocol does not make.

intervalConstruction.attribution: For each statistic, each signal-date cohort's value is written as sum_i w(t,i) Y(t,i) + f(t), with w fixed at the signal date and f a forecast-only term. Y(t,i) is the sum of daily returns over the cohort's H sessions. The contribution of session s is sum over cohorts active at s of sum_i w(t,i) r(s,i) and is attributed to the calendar week containing s; f(t) is attributed to the signal week t. D(w) is the sum of contributions attributed to calendar week w. Summing D over all calendar weeks reproduces the sum of the signal-date statistic exactly, so the estimator and estimand are unchanged.
intervalConstruction.exposureProfile: x(w) = (number of (defined cohort, session) pairs in calendar week w) / H; sum_w x(w) equals the number of defined signal dates.
intervalConstruction.estimate: theta_hat = sum_w D(w) / sum_w x(w), identical to the arithmetic mean of the signal-date statistic over defined dates.
intervalConstruction.normalizer: Residuals e(w) = D(w) - theta_hat x(w); partial sums R(t) = sum_{w<=t} e(w); V = sum_t R(t)^2 over the N calendar weeks.
intervalConstruction.confidenceInterval: theta_hat +/- sqrt(U1CriticalValue * V / N) / sum_w x(w). With x identically one this is exactly v3's interval, which a unit test proves.
intervalConstruction.criticalValueSource: Unchanged from v3: Lobato (2001) U1 pivotal distribution, 97.5% upper critical value 66.57; Shao (2010) recursive-estimate self-normalization, equivalent to Bartlett fixed-b at b=1.
intervalConstruction.undefinedRule: The interval is undefined (never a degenerate zero-width interval) when fewer than two calendar weeks exist, any D or x is non-finite, no signal date is defined, or V <= nearZeroNormalizerRelativeTolerance * N^2 * mean(D^2). Undefined intervals count toward undefinedFrequency.

descriptiveIntervalConstruction.appliesTo: rankIC, and a non-gating disclosure comparator for every confirmatory statistic

undefinedStatistics: A signal date whose statistic is undefined (for example an empty selected set) contributes no cohort weight, no forecast term and no exposure; the date-balanced mean runs over defined dates only. The frozen synthetic designs cannot produce an undefined date; the rule is exercised by unit tests.

acceptance.failureRule: Each metric of each confirmatory statistic in each DGP/depth/horizon cell is classified PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE by monteCarloDecision. A cell takes the worst of its statistics' states (FAIL, then INCONCLUSIVE, then PASS). Do not alter the pivotal critical value, attribution rule, calendar depth, DGP, statistic partition, seed, replicate count, threshold or Monte Carlo decision levels after viewing results under this contract.
acceptance.statusRule: Precedence: (1) INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR if no complete result exists; (2) FAIL if any evaluated confirmatory cell is FAIL; (3) INCONCLUSIVE if any evaluated cell is INCONCLUSIVE; (4) DATA_INSUFFICIENT if any registered cell is below its horizon's minimum confirmatory depth; (5) PASS otherwise. A definite refutation outranks everything; an evaluated cell the simulation cannot resolve outranks an unevaluated one because it is information about the method, whereas a depth shortfall is information about the calendar. Only PASS licenses confirmatory inference; INCONCLUSIVE and DATA_INSUFFICIENT are complete, legitimate results that license nothing.
acceptance.interpretationRule: PASS validates only synthetic null size/coverage behavior of this interval for the confirmatory statistics under these DGPs and depths. It does not establish historical Alpha, profitability, deployability, stationarity or short memory of real returns, or power against economically relevant alternatives.

monteCarloDecision.purpose: Separate three facts that a point-estimate comparison conflates: the truth is on the safe side of a threshold, the truth is on the unsafe side, or the simulation cannot tell. These levels govern ONLY Monte Carlo classification error and are unrelated to the 97.5% level of the statistical interval whose coverage is being measured.
monteCarloDecision.failSideDecisionCountDefinition: registered cells (6 DGPs x 4 horizon/depth pairs = 24) x confirmatory statistics (5) x metrics (coverage, positive false positive, undefined frequency = 3). Each FAIL-side decision therefore uses one-sided alpha 0.05/360.
monteCarloDecision.multiplicityRationale: PASS is an intersection of per-metric claims: a method with even one metric truly on the unsafe side reaches PASS only if that metric's own safe-side bound clears its threshold, which has probability at most the per-metric level, so no adjustment is needed and 0.025 is used per metric. FAIL is a union of per-metric claims, so its familywise false-FAIL probability grows with the number of decisions and is budgeted at 0.05 by Bonferroni. The price is that FAIL is reserved for clear refutation and a moderately deficient method will usually be INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS.
monteCarloDecision.floorMetric: coverage; PASS if lower(passSideAlpha) >= materialCoverageFloor, FAIL if upper(failSideAlpha) < materialCoverageFloor, else INCONCLUSIVE.
monteCarloDecision.ceilingMetrics: positive false-positive rate and undefined frequency; PASS if upper(passSideAlpha) <= ceiling, FAIL if lower(failSideAlpha) > ceiling, else INCONCLUSIVE.
monteCarloDecision.denominators: Coverage and positive false-positive rate are counted over replicates with a defined interval; undefined frequency over all replicates. All counts are integers.
monteCarloDecision.precisionGuard: acceptance.maximumMonteCarlo95HalfWidth is kept as a usability check: an estimate whose 95% half-width exceeds it can never be PASS (it is INCONCLUSIVE with reason MONTE_CARLO_PRECISION_INSUFFICIENT) but can still be FAIL.
monteCarloDecision.noMeasurableReplicates: n = 0 measured replicates is INCONCLUSIVE for coverage and false-positive rate; the undefined-frequency metric of the same statistic is then a FAIL.

stoppingRule: After merge, run 'Synthetic alpha inference calibration v5' exactly once on main. A complete PASS, FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE or DATA_INSUFFICIENT artifact closes this protocol's run budget. v4 is closed and is never rerun. An INCONCLUSIVE v5 is not resolved by rerunning with more replicates or another seed (that is optional stopping): a further precision study would be a NEW preregistered calibration version. A rerun is permitted only when the run produced no complete artifact or reported INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR, after an infrastructure-only repair documented in the result record. A FAIL is never rescued: the inference methodology would be reconsidered in a separately justified future study.

developmentDiagnostics.label: DEVELOPMENT_ONLY
developmentDiagnostics.use: Derivation of the replicate count from the general precision rule, and the exact three-state operating characteristic of the frozen v4 decision rule at generic true-probability values. Computed before this protocol was frozen; uses no simulation of any registered cell, no v4 cell value and no market data. The generic grid was not tuned to any v4 cell.

v4FormalResult.allH126Cells: PASS at 312 and 624 weeks in every DGP

prohibitions: No historical return, label, score, prediction, Alpha result report, signal-history outcome artifact, or Alpha experiment may be read.
No simulation parameter may be estimated from real returns.
v4 is closed: it is never rerun, and its seed, replicate count, thresholds and decision rule are never changed or reinterpreted.
No v1-v4 result may tune a v5 parameter; the replicate count follows from the general precision rule, never from which v4 cell would classify.
The method, DGPs, horizons, depths, statistics, U1 critical value, thresholds and Monte Carlo decision rule are v4's and may not change; a test fails on any scientific difference.
No seed, DGP, tolerance, calendar depth, statistic partition, attribution rule or replicate count may be changed after viewing v5 results under this contract.

The formal run may not be dispatched from a non-main ref, and development smoke runs carry runClass DEVELOPMENT_ONLY, no verdict authority and may not use any closed protocol's seed or the formal seed.
No Alpha model v5 preregistration, seal or execution is created or authorized by this calibration protocol.
